title: Identity federation: sign in with an existing identity

kcs.statement: Identity federation lets users sign in through an external identity provider (a corporate directory, a SAML 2.0 or OIDC provider, or a social login) and receive temporary AWS credentials, so no long-term IAM user is created for each person.
Federation suits large or changing user populations: access is managed in one directory, nobody has long-term AWS keys to rotate, and disabling someone in the directory removes their AWS access.

problem_ideas: A company with 3,000 employees in its corporate directory wants them to reach AWS without new passwords. Pick federation or IAM users and justify the choice.
An employee leaves on Friday. Compare the offboarding steps with 3,000 IAM users and with federation.
Which kind of credential does a federated user receive: an access key pair, temporary credentials or a root password?
Match each identity source (Google login, a SAML 2.0 corporate IdP, an OIDC provider) to the federation it supports.
Spot the anti-pattern: a team creates one shared IAM user and gives its keys to 20 contractors.
Explain what single sign-on means for a user who needs 5 AWS accounts and 3 SaaS apps.
